title.narrative: LA Nina Anticipatory Action Allocation (Provision of Nutrition lifesaving support to communities with high intersectoral severity in Dinsor District of Bay Region)

description.narrative: ltpgtDue to drought and limited access to essential services, population in Diinsor district is under-served. Children, pregnant and lactating mothers face unimaginable challenges such as acute malnutrition, disease outbreak, and displacement . The proposed nutrition program by MARDO in Dinsoor is designed to tackle the urgent and escalating crisis of acute malnutrition, which is expected to worsen due to the impacts of La Niña. With projections indicating that approximately 1.7 million children under five in Somalia will face acute malnutrition in 2024. moreover, according to MARDO quarterly report indicated that admissions among children under age five rose significantly in Q1 2023 compared to previous years due to impact of drought in 2022. for example, in Q1 2023, 31% of the target under-five five and PLW reached higher than any achievement in 2022 and 2021. Also, the same trends are expected in Q1 2025 if we don't act now and scale anticipatory nutrition interventions along with treatment for those children and mothers in need to prevent death due to hunger and malnutrition. MARDO is positioning itself to intervene immediately, scale, and sustain essential nutrition services for the drought-affected vulnerable populations through inpatient care by strengthening 1 stabilization center, 2 fixed OTP/TSFP and 2 mobile teams covering 7 villages Waaberi SC/OTP/TSFP fixed site, Tini IDP fixed site OTP/TSFP site, Mobile team (1) Balila 1 OTP/TSFP site, Mobile team (1) Balila 2, Mobile team (2) Raami Dhaw, Mobile team (2) Yaaqshiid, Mobile team (2) QODQOD). worst affected by drought and AWD reaching additional 12,250 beneficiaries, including 5,250 women, 3250 girls, 3250 boy, 500 men, and the wider community. Training community health workers (CHWs) for nutrition screening, referrals, and broader health needs. This will establish a community-based early warning system for nutrition for shock prevention. The program will also promote MIYCN through community-based interventions, utilizing social behavior change (SBC) strategies to empower families with essential knowledge about appropriate feeding practices. Educational initiatives will focus on the importance of breastfeeding, dietary diversity, and proper complementary feeding. Additionally, the program will incorporate initiatives to promote nutrition-sensitive agriculture and household food production, including the “one egg per child per day” campaign, which encourages families to produce their own food, thereby improving dietary diversity and nutritional intake. MARDO has both PD and FLA with UNICEF and WFP, which will ensure easy access to nutritional supplies and commodities, improving coverage and complementarity /synergies so that affected beneficiaries receive a comprehensive package of services. MARDO will provide micronutrient supplementation for children under five and pregnant and breastfeeding women, addressing critical nutritional deficiencies that can have serious health implications. Essential protection measures will be integrated into the program to ensure a holistic approach. These include Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), Prevention of sexual exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Gender-Based Violence (GBV) considerations, and Child Protection initiatives. By embedding these protective measures within the nutrition program, MARDO aims to create a safe and supportive environment for all beneficiaries.ltbrgtlt/pgt
